Shipment Data Architecture: Entities, Relational Models & Schemas

14 min read Updated: November 2026 By Rajvardhan Singh Rathore
Modeling freight data requires balancing high-frequency streaming events with immutable physical assets. This comprehensive guide outlines the entity relationships, PostgreSQL schemas, and indexing strategies for global freight platforms.

The Logistics Domain Entity Hierarchy

To accurately capture freight movements across ocean carriers, air waybills, customs brokers, and last-mile vans, data models must decouple the physical container or parcel from the commercial order:

  • Order (Commercial): The buyer/seller agreement with line items, purchase order numbers, and declared value.
  • Shipment (Logistical Master): The operational movement of goods between origin and destination under a master bill of lading (BOL).
  • Package / Unit / Container: The physical serialized vessel (pallet, 40ft dry container, parcel box).
  • Tracking Milestone / Status Event: The immutable point-in-time telemetry record capturing timestamp, location, and operational state.

Production PostgreSQL DDL Specification

The following production schema implements foreign-key constraints, UUIDv7 primary keys, and JSONB payload metadata support:

PostgreSQL DDL 
-- Master Shipments Table
CREATE TABLE master_shipments (
  shipment_id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
  shipper_account_id UUID NOT NULL,
  master_tracking_number VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL,
  carrier_scac VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
  transport_mode VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL CHECK (transport_mode IN ('PARCEL', 'LTL', 'FTL', 'OCEAN_FCL', 'OCEAN_LCL', 'AIR_FREIGHT')),
  current_status VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'ORDER_CREATED',
  
  -- Geographic Endpoints
  origin_unlocode CHAR(5),
  origin_postal_code VARCHAR(20),
  destination_unlocode CHAR(5),
  destination_postal_code VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
  
  -- Physical cargo constraints
  total_packages INT NOT NULL CHECK (total_packages >= 1),
  declared_weight_kg NUMERIC(10, 2) NOT NULL CHECK (declared_weight_kg > 0),
  volumetric_weight_kg NUMERIC(10, 2),
  
  -- Timestamps
  estimated_delivery_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  actual_delivery_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

-- Milestone Events (Immutable Telemetry Log)
CREATE TABLE shipment_milestone_events (
  event_id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
  shipment_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES master_shipments(shipment_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  carrier_event_code VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
  canonical_status VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
  event_timestamp TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  ingested_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  
  -- Spatial data
  facility_code VARCHAR(30),
  location_name VARCHAR(100),
  latitude NUMERIC(9, 6),
  longitude NUMERIC(9, 6),
  
  -- Raw carrier audit payload
  raw_carrier_payload JSONB
);

Table Partitioning & High-Throughput Indexing

In high-scale logistics platforms processing > 50 million events per month, shipment_milestone_events is range-partitioned by event_timestamp on a monthly cadence:

CREATE TABLE shipment_milestone_events (
  ...
) PARTITION BY RANGE (event_timestamp);

CREATE TABLE events_2026_11 PARTITION OF shipment_milestone_events
  FOR VALUES FROM ('2026-11-01 00:00:00+00') TO ('2026-12-01 00:00:00+00');

Composite B-tree indexes are added on (shipment_id, event_timestamp DESC) to accelerate the latest-status query pattern.

Multimodal vs Last-Mile Data Modeling

Ocean and intermodal freight involve intermediate transshipment hubs, vessel IMO numbers, and container seals, while last-mile parcel networks track courier driver geofence proximity and recipient delivery signatures. Discover more in our Shipment Lifecycle State Machine Guide.
